title: Restriction and trace of a finite etale morphism
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $F$ an abelian sheaf on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$, i.e. $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]; let $f^{-1}:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ and $f_*:\Ab(Y_{\Et})\to\Ab(X_{\Et})$ be the inverse and direct image, $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ with unit $\eta_f$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

1. The *restriction* of $f$ at $F$ is the morphism of abelian sheaves $\operatorname{res}_{f,F}=\eta_{f}(F):F\to f_*f^{-1}F$, the component at $F$ of the unit of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$.
2. The *trace* of $f$ at $F$ is the morphism of abelian sheaves $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ which is the member at $(f,F)$ of the unique family $(\operatorname{tr}_{f,F})_{f,F}$, indexed by all finite etale morphisms $f$ and all $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, that [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists] provides: the family that is (0) natural in $F$, (1) compatible with etale localization on $X$, and (2) equal to the sum map $F^{\oplus d}\to F$ under $f_*f^{-1}F=F^{\oplus d}$ when $Y=\coprod_{i=1}^dX$ and $f$ is the identity on each summand.

When $F$ is a sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules ($n\ge1$), $\operatorname{res}_{f,F}$ and $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$ are taken on the underlying abelian sheaf; $f^{-1}F$ and $f_*f^{-1}F$ are again killed by $n$, so both maps are maps of sheaves of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules (see the last construction step).

source.place: Stacks Definition 03SE (definition-trace-map) and the paragraphs around it in Section 03SH (section-trace-method)

proof.text: *Restriction.* $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ on abelian sheaves is part of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] (with $f_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]); $\operatorname{res}_{f,F}$ is its unit at $F$, as in Stacks Section 03SH: 'The adjunction map $\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^{-1}$ is called restriction.' Nothing beyond the adjunction is used; finiteness and etaleness of $f$ play no role here.

*Trace: choice of formulation.* Stacks first describes the trace as the counit $f_!f^{-1}\to\mathrm{id}$ of $f_!\dashv f^{-1}$, transported along $f_!\cong f_*$ (Lemma 03S7, `lemma-shriek-equals-star-finite-etale`, line 11571, whose proof is itself 'omitted' in the split case), and then says: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties: (1) it commutes with etale localization on $X$ and (2) if $Y=\coprod_{i=1}^dX$ then the trace map is the sum map ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given; in particular we do not need to know about the existence of $f_!$ and the agreement of $f_!$ with $f_*$ in order to construct the trace map.' The DAG follows this second formulation: it is the one the DAG supports, since [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists] states existence and uniqueness of the characterized family, while the DAG has $v_!$ for etale $v$ only as the imported, unsplit [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] (unit sk-thm-iff, with its adjunction in the imported lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives) and no node for the comparison $f_!\to f_*$ (Stacks 0F4L) or its invertibility for finite etale $f$; [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] covers open immersions only. The identification of the trace with the counit of $f_!\dashv f^{-1}$ is not used by any node and is not stated.

proof.text: *Trace: the definition.* Given $f$ finite etale and $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists] gives a family $(\operatorname{tr}_{f',F'})$ over all finite etale $f':Y'\to X'$ and all $F'\in\Ab(X'_{\Et})$ with properties (0), (1), (2), and says it is the only such family. Set $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$ to be its member at $(f,F)$. By uniqueness this does not depend on any choice (in particular not on the etale covering trivializing $f$ used to construct it), so $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$ is well defined; it is a morphism of abelian sheaves $f_*f^{-1}F\to F$, natural in $F$.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), line 10333 ff., Definition 03SE (definition-trace-map, line 10353) and the paragraph after it

proof.text: *Linearity for $\mathbf Z/n$-coefficients.* Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathbf Z/n$-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Then $n\cdot\mathrm{id}_F=0$, and since $f^{-1}$ and $f_*$ are additive, $n\cdot\mathrm{id}=0$ on $f^{-1}F$ and on $f_*f^{-1}F$; an abelian group killed by $n$ has exactly one $\mathbf Z/n$-module structure, and every additive map between such groups is $\mathbf Z/n$-linear; so on every etale $W\to X$ the components of $\operatorname{res}_{f,F}$ and $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$ are $\mathbf Z/n$-linear. (For a general ring $R$ and a sheaf of $R$-modules, $R$-linearity of both maps would follow from naturality of $\eta_f$ and property (0) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists] applied to the endomorphism $r\cdot$ of $F$, $r\in R$; no node uses this, so it is not stated.)

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks Section 03SH (Definition 03SE, the characterization paragraph, Lemma lemma-shriek-equals-star-finite-etale). The statement now says exactly which objects res and tr are: res is the unit of f^{-1} -| f_*; tr is the member at (f,F) of the unique family of lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-exists (Stacks' characterization, which Stacks itself says suffices to define the trace without f_!). Stacks' primary description as the counit of f_! -| f^{-1} transported along f_! = f_* was not followed: the DAG has v_! for etale v only as the imported unsplit def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension and no node for f_! = f_* (def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero is for open immersions). The R-linearity claim was removed from the statement as a claim; the Z/n case is justified in an elementary construction step (additive maps of groups killed by n are Z/n-linear), which is all lemma-weil-pbc-curve-locally-constant-reduction step 6 uses; the general-R case (from naturality) is recorded but not stated as a node since nothing uses it. Added def-weil-pbc-etale-site to stmt_deps. Mathlib searches extended by loogle, a second leanfinder, a leansearch and a grep on f_!/trace: no match.
